title: M Arisa: high density, but facilities that feel far above its price.
excerpt: A freehold project of 1,500 units off Jalan Sentul, priced around RM300,000 to RM500,000. Sean is impressed by the sky garden and facilities deck at this price, but warns of density, lost views and strained roads.
takeaways: A 708 sq ft two-bedroom bought at about RM420,000 rents for about RM1,800 to RM2,000 furnished.
Twelve lifts serve 30 units a floor, and a sky garden and facilities deck link the two towers.
Empty plots in front will block some KL skyline views, and Sentul's roads are already crowded.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: M Arisa is a freehold project of 1,500 units in two towers joined by an elevated car park, a facilities floor and a rooftop sky garden with halal and non-halal barbecue areas. The towers rise straight to the ground without a transfer structure, so the deck between them can be free-form: a stream crossing the landscaping, a playground, a glass-walled hall, a games room and co-working space, and a gym in a UFO-shaped pavilion with Technogym equipment. Twelve lifts serve 30 units a floor, the fire doors stay open on magnets, a refuse chute is built in, and air-conditioner ledges have safety rails.

Sean viewed a 708 sq ft two-bedroom, two-bathroom Type C: an open kitchen with the washer built in, no yard, two similar-sized bedrooms, laminated floors, tinted windows, a KL skyline view, and a common bathroom placed on the facade rather than the void.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The project sits off Jalan Sentul, which is lined with about five schools, churches, temples and a market and gets congested at peak times. The DUKE highway now offers an alternative route, Sentul Point's shops and eateries are within walking distance, and the surrounding area is still mostly old landed housing. The developer's earlier M Centura stands beside it, and empty plots in front are likely to become high-rises.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: This unit was bought for about RM420,000 at launch, and fully furnished units rent for about RM1,800 to RM2,000 a month depending on orientation. Prices across the project ranged from about RM300,000 to RM500,000.

standout.title: Free-form spaces between straight towers
standout.body: Because both residential towers run straight from roof to ground, the lighter car park and facility structure between them is freed from their column grid. That lets the deck curve and layer, with a stream, raised playgrounds and a floating gym pavilion, and the link between towers reduces the gap they need.

pros: The balance of price, experience, value and connectivity: a product like this at RM300,000 to RM500,000 is hard to beat.

Genuine design: a concrete wall instead of fencing, a sky garden on arrival, straight towers that free the facilities deck, a tidy unit grid, plenty of lifts, magnetic fire doors, no units facing each other directly, and even safety rails for aircon installers.
Continuous improvement: having reviewed the developer's projects across eras, he sees it keep what works and drop what doesn't, and the pride shows.
cons: Density: 1,500 units here, plus neighbouring high-density projects by the same developer and others, although the wider area is still low-rise landed housing.
Uncertain views: the empty land in front will most likely become another high-rise, so a promised KLCC view may not last, though DUKE gives an alternative route.
Infrastructure: Sentul's roads, schools and shops are already strained, with double parking and congestion, and handover took a while because 1,500 owners queued for keys.

closing: A remarkably well-designed high-density home near the city at a mass-market price, for buyers who can live with crowds and changing views.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this November 2025 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view the unit after handover; the purchase price and rents are as he quoted them.
